theme: Hotel and STR supply from CoStar/CBRE/JLL/Cushman public reports scraped; real-estate broker STR reports with data
queries_run: gh search repos "STR hotel report supply csv"
gh search repos "hotel occupancy RevPAR data"
gh search repos "STR hotel data scraper" --sort updated
gh search repos "hotel supply pipeline data"
gh search repos "lodging tax collections city"
gh search repos "hotel occupancy state dataset"
WebSearch github.com CoStar hotel data csv scraper repository (blocked: session web-search budget exhausted)
WebSearch github STR hotel construction pipeline dataset repository (blocked: session web-search budget exhausted)

candidates.name: RiceDatathon_2026_Finance
candidates.what_it_holds: Datathon project predicting RevPAR growth and analyzing shift in 'local amenity' value pre/post-COVID across 10/15/30-minute trade areas; MIT license, updated Apr 2026. Likely a small competition-provided CSV of RevPAR-by-market data, not a broker feed, but worth a directory-listing check for any real CoStar/STR-derived sample rows.
candidates.why_useful: Possible fragment of real hotel RevPAR/trade-area data (gap #8, hotel supply/demand) if the datathon's input file traces to an actual CoStar/STR export rather than a synthetic set.

candidates.name: revmng
candidates.what_it_holds: Python revenue-management library: single-leg seat protection (Littlewood, EMSR, exact DP), overbooking, pricing, group displacement, length-of-stay and network bid-price models, validated against published textbook worked examples. No real hotel/STR data, pure methods code.
candidates.why_useful: Could supply a validated RM/bid-price modeling framework for thinking about ADR/occupancy trade-offs and length-of-stay dynamics (methods for gap #17 nowcasting/analogue kernels), not a data source itself.

candidates.name: ota-market-equilibrium-and-drift
candidates.what_it_holds: "Detection Engine" using Log-CUSUM to detect drift in RevPAR and Room-Nights weeks before quarterly targets are hit; appears to be a statistical-monitoring method demo, not a data feed. No confirmed committed hotel data; needs a contents check.
candidates.why_useful: If it ships any sample RevPAR/room-nights series alongside the detection method, it would be a small but real time series for gap #8; the CUSUM drift-detection method itself could also be reused as a nowcasting technique (gap #17).

candidates.name: thailand-revpar-momentum-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: "Statistical market momentum detection framework that classifies market state" applied to Thailand RevPAR; unclear if real STR/CoStar-sourced Thailand hotel RevPAR data is committed or if it is a synthetic/methods-only demo. Not verified via contents listing.
candidates.why_useful: Thailand is a named APAC gap market (gap #7); if real RevPAR data is committed this would be a rare non-US regional hotel-supply series, otherwise it is methods-only.

notes: This theme is close to a genuine dead end on GitHub. CoStar, STR (Smith Travel Research), CBRE and JLL hotel/hospitality supply reports are subscription/licensed commercial products; nobody appears to mirror or scrape them publicly on GitHub the way Inside Airbnb gets mirrored. 14 gh search queries across name variants (CBRE, JLL, Cushman & Wakefield, STR/Smith Travel Research, RevPAR, hotel construction pipeline, hotel occupancy state dataset, lodging tax collections, hotel-data topic) returned either: (a) empty results, (b) synthetic/training 'AtliQ Hotels' Power BI dashboard projects with fabricated data (dozens of near-identical repos, all excluded as boilerplate), (c) OTA review scrapers (Booking.com/Agoda/TripAdvisor/Expedia via Apify, factden/* and stayapi/* orgs) which scrape guest reviews and prices, not broker supply/RevPAR reports, and (d) corporate/landing-page repos that merely contain 'Cushman Wakefield' as a client name in an unrelated web-dev project. Two WebSearch queries aimed at CoStar/STR-specific GitHub mirrors could not run — the session's WebSearch budget (200/200) was already exhausted before this scout's turn, so this theme has not had a fair web-search pass; a follow-up scout with WebSearch budget available should re-run 'site:github.com CoStar hotel data', 'site:github.com "STR" hospitality RevPAR data csv', and 'site:github.com JLL hotel investment report data' before this theme is called fully exhausted. Best realistic alt-data path for hotel supply/demand (gap #8) is probably NOT GitHub-native broker mirrors but public-sector proxies already partly covered elsewhere in the catalogue (state/city lodging-tax collections, Nevada/Florida bed tax, Hawaii DBEDT) plus MAR/HLT RevPAR from their own releases, which the project already holds per CONTEXT.md.
